passing_case_counts` is shared by every surface, but the new vitest-JSON branch now applies per-assertion counts for all surfaces, not just `native`. `cli` and `api` have no runner filter in `SURFACE_RUNNERS`, so a staged Jest/vitest report in the same run now inflates the `cases` total that backs `tests_run` for a `cli` run (previously each vitest id counted as 1). Since the check is `cases < tests_run → fail`, this inflation can mask a short-count `cli`/`api` block that previously failed — a silent loosening of an existing gate.
findings.suggestion: Apply the per-assertion vitest counting only when the surface is `native` (thread the surface through, or gate the branch on it), or add a regression test asserting a `cli` block with `tests_run` larger than the pytest passing count still fails when a vitest report is also staged.

findings.file: shared/scripts/tools/verifiers/_surface_runner.py (junit loop followed by `counts.update(... vitest ...)`) and the docs claim in plugins/shipwright-iterate/skills/iterate/references/F0.5.md ("staging both is counted once, as the larger")
findings.finding: When the same test id appears in both the JUnit and vitest case-count dicts, `counts.update` makes the vitest count win unconditionally, not the larger of the two. The documented rule ("the larger") and the `_case_count` max-over-labels logic can therefore disagree with the per-id counts for duplicate ids (e.g. a jest-junit report without describe-prefixed names producing ids identical to the JSON ones).
findings.suggestion: Merge with max (`counts[tid] = max(counts.get(tid, 0), n)`) or drop the "as the larger" wording; add a test where JUnit carries a higher per-id count than the JSON.

findings.finding: When a touched native package is the repo root (`directory == ""`), every project-relative JS/TS result in the staged report counts, including results belonging to other (non-touched, possibly non-native) directories in the same repo, and `uncovered_root` is satisfied by any one passing result anywhere. This is only a whole-repo-package scenario so exposure is small, but it means `tests_run` for a root-package native run can be backed by results outside any UI-bearing directory.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable if intentional (single-package repo); if not, document it or require the passing results to at least be JS/TS under the repo (which they are) — but a one-line comment pinning the `root == ""` semantics would prevent future "fixes" in either direction.

findings.finding: This test is byte-for-byte the same scenario as `test_native_ui_diff_passes_with_jest_json_under_the_package` (same fixture via `native_repo`, same staging, same assertion); it does not actually exercise the "new in this diff" merge-base branch any differently — `FILES` puts `package.json` in the branch commit in both tests, and there is no distinct assertion on the new-file path. The genuinely new-file cases live in the gates file, so coverage exists, but this test's name promises something it doesn't pin.
findings.suggestion: Either delete it or make it distinct (e.g. assert the base-side check ran, or add a new file rather than the package manifest case it claims).  Non-findings I checked deliberately: the `Tests:`-line-only filter for `parse_tests_run` (AC1) is correctly implemented and tested including ANSI codes; the kinds/labels split is pinned by an explicit test; path traversal (`../`), Windows drive/UNC, and sibling-prefix (`apps/mobile-admin`) containment are all tested; the merge-base relabel attacks (nested manifest added, nested web manifest deleted, browser file claimed by a new manifest) each have a dedicated test; AC5 refusal text and both docs files state the recipe including the `file` attribute.

findings.finding: Directory containment does not establish package ownership. Tests in a nested, separate package such as `apps/mobile/web/package.json` count as evidence for touched UI in `apps/mobile`, even if that nested package is web-only. This violates AC4’s requirement that another package’s results never satisfy native evidence.
findings.suggestion: Resolve each result file’s nearest package at the verified commit and require that package to be one of the touched native packages. Add a test with a nested package whose passing results are the only staged evidence.

findings.finding: Taking the maximum count across report formats undercounts distinct tests. If touched package A supplies two Jest JSON assertions and touched package B supplies two different JUnit cases, both packages have valid evidence, but `tests_run=4` fails because this returns two.
findings.suggestion: Deduplicate overlapping executions rather than treating all reports in different formats as duplicates. Preserve the sum for distinct package results and test a mixed-format, two-package run.  Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The implementation covers the main native flow, but package attribution and mixed-format counting need correction before shipping.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
